reuse.why: All affected consumers reuse applyWeekendRule and the existing recurrence conversion, although occurrence selection remains separately implemented.

duplication.why: The budget helper removes repeated adjustment code, but the upcoming and range handlers duplicate the adjustment, null filtering, and day conversion block.

placement.why: Holiday matching and date adjustment remain in shared/schedules.ts, while handler registration and budget accumulation stay in their established server layers.

scope.why: The edits focus on the requested scheduling rules, range handler, configuration data, and related tests.

maintainability.why: The central adjustment helper is clear, but separate seven-occurrence, count-times-seven, and two-day bounds scatter assumptions about its policy across consumers.

bypasses_abstraction.where: The changed scheduling consumers all delegate weekend and holiday adjustment to applyWeekendRule.

disguised_duplication.where: The duplicated occurrence-to-day transformation in the two schedule handlers is explicit rather than disguised.

abstraction_drift.where: WeekendRule gains frequency and holidays, and applyWeekendRule gains a daily-frequency branch; consumers continue using the helper.
